 Legendary Patrol badge returns to the U.S.: Nissan introduces Armada Patrol PRO-4X grade
 Legendary Patrol badge returns to the U.S.: Nissan introduces Armada Patrol PRO-4X grade
 Renamed PRO-4X grade and new adventure-ready accessories celebrate 75 years of Patrol heritage 
 Save 
 Remove 
 Download 
 Share
 Subscribe 
 Photos / Galleries / Videos 
 November 9, 2026
 NASHVILLE, Tenn. – Nissan is reintroducing the legendary Patrol nameplate to the U.S. for the first time since 1969, bringing one of the brand's most enduring and globally recognized badges back to American roads.
 For the 2027 model year, Armada's capable PRO-4X grade is renamed Patrol PRO-4X 1 , aligning the model with Patrol's 75-year heritage of global SUV adventure. Production for the newly named grade starts in November 2026.
 2027 Armada Patrol PRO-4X 
 Previous Next 
 Armada Patrol PRO‑4X also expands its adventure-ready offering with newly added NISMO rock sliders and a NISMO roof rack, arriving this winter, alongside available NISMO Axis wheels paired with BFGoodrich all-terrain tires.
 "Patrol has defined adventure for 75 years, earning its reputation on some of the toughest terrain in the world. Bringing the Nissan Patrol name back to America through Armada is a natural fit, with both vehicles sharing the same iconic and proven platform," said Tiago Castro , senior vice president, U.S. Marketing & Sales, Nissan and INFINITI. "Armada Patrol PRO‑4X honors that legendary heritage while carrying its capability and confidence into Nissan's future."
 The Armada Patrol PRO-4X will see its public debut on Nissan's stand at the 2026 LA Auto Show (November 20-29).
 Armada Patrol PRO-4X with accessories 
 A 75-year legacy of global adventure 
 Patrol has been part of the Nissan lineup since 1951 and stands as one of the company's longest-running and most iconic nameplates. Across seven generations, Patrol has established itself globally as the go-to vehicle for adventure and exploration.
 It was also the first Nissan-badged vehicle sold in America, beginning in 1962, helping establish Nissan's reputation as an adventurous, challenger brand that empowers drivers to get more out of every journey.
 Armada Patrol PRO-4X builds on that legacy with a nameplate backed by 75 years of global credibility. It continues to offer all the equipment that enables Armada PRO-4X to tackle varied terrain , including an electronic locking rear differential, Adaptive Electronic Air Suspension 2 , all-terrain tires, eight selectable drive modes, a metal underbody skid plate and advanced camera systems like Invisible Hood View 3 .

 An Armada for virtually every adventure 
 All versions of the 2027 Nissan Armada empower owners with elevated on-road comfort and effortless capability off-road. Owners enjoy the confidence of knowing that nine out of every 10 Armada SUVs sold in the last decade are still on the road 5 . The 2026 Armada was named a segment winner in the J.D. Power 2026 U.S. Automotive Performance, Execution and Layout (APEAL) Study , a Consumer Reports Top-Rated Large SUV 6 and Best Large SUV for Off-Roading in the 2026 U.S. News & World Report Best Adventure Vehicles Awards .
 For the 2027 model year, Armada also adds a Dark Armor package that complements the SUV's bold stance with a distinctive, more aggressive blacked-out appearance. The Dark Armor darkens Armada's roof rails, window trim, front grille and lower fascia, paired with black 20-inch wheels and black exterior badges. Armada's interior adds black upholstery, a panoramic moonroof and darkened accents for the dashboard, steering wheel and center console.
 For details on all features and specifications for the 2027 Nissan Armada, as well as photos and videos, see the full press kit . Consumers can learn more and register for updates here .
 Q&A 
 Q: Why is Nissan changing the name of the Armada PRO-4X to the Armada Patrol PRO-4X? 
 A: Nissan is bringing the legendary Patrol name back to the U.S. for the first time in more than 50 years. The Patrol name has represented rugged capability, durability and adventure around the world since 1951, and it was also the first Nissan-badged vehicle sold in America. By renaming Armada PRO-4X to Armada Patrol PRO-4X, Nissan is connecting Armada's proven off-road capability with 75 years of Patrol heritage and global recognition. Armada remains the vehicle nameplate, while Patrol identifies the model's most adventure-focused grade and reinforces its connection to one of Nissan's most iconic SUV legends.
 Q: Is the Nissan Armada good for going off-road? 
 A: The Nissan Armada was rigorously designed and tested to give drivers confident performance off-road. The Armada Patrol PRO-4X features all-terrain tires, an off-road-specific front bumper with an increased approach angle, underbody skid plates, an electronic locking differential and Adaptive Electronic Air Suspension 7 . It stands out from other SUVs at the trailhead with fender flares, 20-inch painted PRO-4X wheels and numerous Lava Red accents.
 Q: What safety technologies are on the Nissan Armada? 
 A: The Nissan Armada features standard Nissan Safety Shield® 360 8 , including Automatic Emergency Braking with Pedestrian Detection, High Beam Assist, Blind Spot Warning, Lane Departure Warning, Rear Automatic Braking and Rear Cross Traffic Alert, plus Intelligent Forward Collision Warning, Intelligent Blind Spot Intervention and Intelligent Lane Intervention.
 Q: Is the Nissan Armada good for towing? 
 A: Armada has a standard towing capacity of up to 8,500 pounds 9 , with a Class IV tow hitch and 7-pin harness/pre-wiring on all grades plus standard Trailer Blind Spot Monitoring 10 .
 Q: How spacious is the Nissan Armada? 
 A: The Nissan Armada has three rows of seating and accommodates up to eight passengers, depending on seating position. Cargo room behind the third row is 20.4 cubic feet, 56.3 cubic feet behind the second row and 97.1 cubic feet behind the first row 11 . Maximum cargo area dimensions measure 84.7 inches long, 51.7 inches wide and 35.6 inches tall.
